title: PersonaClaims type is bypassed by ad-hoc json!, and the two shapes already disagree
description:
persona-core/src/hvid.rs defines `PersonaClaims` and `PresenceInfo` as the typed wire shape of the `persona` JWT extension — documented as "Serialises to the exact JSON shape required by the spec", re-exported from persona-core/src/lib.rs:15, and covered by two round-trip tests.

Nothing constructs them. The one place that emits the extension, persona-grpc/src/service.rs:162-173, hand-builds it with `serde_json::json!` instead, and the two shapes have already drifted apart:

| field | PersonaClaims (hvid.rs) | service.rs json! |
|---|---|---|
| `presence.attested_at` | `String`, documented "RFC 3339 timestamp" (hvid.rs:14) | `now_secs`, a `u64` of Unix seconds (service.rs:169) |
| `presence.present_until` | `String`, RFC 3339 (hvid.rs:16) | `u64` Unix seconds (service.rs:170) |
| `identity_assurance` | `IdentityAssurance` enum, serialises `"iaa2"` | `claim.assurance.to_string()` — same text today, but by coincidence of two independent impls |
| `sources` / `auth_methods` | `Vec<String>` | `[&claim.source]` — always exactly one element |

So the tokens personad actually issues do not match the type that claims to define the format, and the compiler cannot see the mismatch. Any future field added to `PersonaClaims` silently will not appear in issued tokens; any consumer written against `PersonaClaims` will fail to deserialise a real token's `attested_at`.

The ponytail comment at service.rs:155 flags the seconds-vs-RFC-3339 choice as deliberate, but the resolution belongs in `PresenceInfo` (change the field types, or make them a typed timestamp), not in a parallel untyped literal.

Fix: build `PersonaClaims` in service.rs and `serde_json::to_value` it. That makes the divergence a compile error and deletes the hand-written JSON.
close_reason: Fixed in 4f63194: service.rs builds PersonaClaims and serialises it; the json! literal is gone. No wire change, verified by a scratch program comparing old literal vs typed path over identical inputs. PersonaClaims gained an inherent new() because #[non_exhaustive] blocks cross-crate literals; the attribute was kept (nine sites in persona-core). New test's oracle is SPEC-HIA.md, mutation-verified. NOTE: the bead's divergence table was partly stale -- hvid.rs already declared attested_at/present_until as u64, so no RFC 3339 mismatch existed.
